fields.verbatim_quote: we actively combat software piracy, but we continue to lose revenue due to illegal use of our software. Third parties may illegally copy and sell counterfeit versions of our products. To the extent counterfeit installations and sales replace otherwise legitimate ones, our operating results could be adversely affected.

due to challenges in detecting patent infringement pertaining to generative AI technologies, it may be more difficult to protect our generative AI and related innovations with patents. Additionally, if we use generative AI in the creation of our source code, we may not be able to rely on copyright to protect such intellectual property.

Lower sales and subscriptions, reduced demand for our products, services and solutions, and increases in our attrition rate in any given period may not be fully reflected in our results of operations until future periods.

fields.verbatim_quote: we collect and store information on behalf of our business customers and if our customers fail to comply with contractual obligations or applicable laws, it could result in litigation or reputational harm to us.

We test goodwill for impairment at least annually. We review our goodwill and intangible assets for impairment when events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value may not be recoverable, including declines in stock price, market capitalization or reduced future cash flow estimates and slower growth rates in our industry.

Our senior unsecured notes, commercial paper program and revolving credit agreement impose restrictions on us and require us to maintain compliance with specified covenants. Our ability to comply with these covenants may be affected by events beyond our control. If we breach any of the covenants and do not obtain a waiver from the noteholders or lenders, then, subject to applicable cure periods, any outstanding debt may be declared immediately due and payable.

These laws, regulations and codes may also impact our innovation and business drivers in developing new and emerging technologies (for example, AI and machine learning) and may impact demand for our offerings and force us to bear the burden of more onerous obligations in our contracts.

Key findings: (1) Figma acquisition termination: Adobe incurred a $1B termination fee in Q1 FY2024 (nine months ended August 30, 2024) for the failed Figma acquisition—noted as a one-time cost but not SIFI-material. (2) Debt and capital: Adobe has $6.15B in senior notes outstanding, a $1.5B revolving credit facility (undrawn), and a $3B commercial paper program (undrawn). These are standard corporate financing arrangements. (3) Third-party dependencies: Adobe discloses reliance on third-party hosting, data center facilities, and cloud infrastructure providers for its cloud solutions and AI inferencing costs, but does not name specific counterparties or disclose material concentrations. (4) No customer concentration disclosures above 10% are mentioned. (5) No related-party arrangements or off-balance-sheet entities are disclosed. (6) AI risk: Adobe acknowledges risks from generative AI development, regulatory exposure (EU AI Act), and competition from other generative AI offerings, but these are standard risk disclosures without SIFI-material specifics. No hidden leverage, circularity, revenue roundtripping, capex ROI gaps, execution risks, or cost opacity patterns are identified in this section. The Figma termination fee is the only concrete transaction mentioned and does not meet the SIFI threshold for extraction."
